claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the model for launch is compliant on the current record because aggregate readiness, rehearsal results, limited rollout, rollback capability, and public governance guidance are sufficient despite an exposed health-plan benefits support weakness.
decision_criteria: If the affected use case is excluded from rollout, the policy concern materially changes.
If there is approved risk acceptance expressly covering the exposed health-plan benefits support weakness, the certification basis materially strengthens.

If there is a reviewed final disclosure artifact covering the material limitation for the named launch use case, the action may become compliant or compliant_with_caveats depending on the rest of the record.
Without exclusion, approved risk acceptance, or evidenced disclosure, certification remains insufficiently supported under the stated policy.
evidence_requests: Provide the final model-card or launch disclosure artifact showing explicit disclosure of the health-plan benefits support limitation for the named launch use case.
Provide reviewed and approved risk-acceptance documentation if the claim is that launch may proceed despite continued exposure.
Provide the underlying internal policy text or release checklist showing disclosure-backed certification is permitted when a material limitation is unresolved but disclosed.
Provide evidence showing whether the initial rollout cohort does or does not include the affected health-plan benefits support use case.
specific_concerns: The actor summary itself says the health-plan benefits support segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The policy text says rollout controls and monitoring do not cure a material model-card weakness when the affected segment remains exposed unless there is reviewed risk acceptance.
The available risk-acceptance draft is described as incomplete, with a blank approver line and no stated treatment of the exposed health-plan benefits support weakness.
No admissible evidence is provided showing that the required model-card disclosure has actually been prepared, reviewed, or attached to launch materials.
Public AI-governance sources may support documentation and monitoring in general, but they do not by themselves satisfy the case-specific policy predicate for this launch.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the current record absent evidence of approved risk acceptance or completed disclosure artifacts.
That rollout at 3% with a rollback switch materially resolves the policy issue for an exposed affected segment.
That public model-card and NIST-style guidance, by themselves, supply sufficient support for this specific internal certification decision.
